Hai Ông Già, Một Ấm Trà: Two Old Men, One Pot of Tea
Hôm qua ông Khải ở tiệm sách mang sang c: Yesterday Mr. Khải from the bookshop brought over his late wife’s wall clock. Its hands had stopped years ago.
Bác sửa cả buổi chiều, ông ngồi bên cạnh: I spent the whole afternoon on it while he sat beside me reading aloud. Two old men, one table, one pot of tea, and it felt like a festival. When the hands finally moved again, Mr. Khải stood very still for a long while before he smiled.
Em ơi, cô Hạnh nhờ chị sáng thứ Bảy nào: Ms. Hạnh asked me to bring a small bunch of flowers every Saturday morning, to stand on her piano for the music class.
Đổi lại, bé Na với tụi nhỏ ghé tiệm đàn: In return, Na and the kids come by the shop and play me a song on a toy trumpet. People walking past stop to listen, and some even buy a bunch to take home. I call it “flowers for music”. The kids love it.
Tấm Biển Có Vết Sơn: The Sign with a Paint Stain
Mình với cậu họa sĩ tầng trên vừa sơn lạ: The painter upstairs and I just repainted the sign for Mr. Khải’s bookshop. He did the lettering, I held the ladder and… knocked over half a tin of green paint.
Tưởng bị mắng, ai ngờ ông Khải cười bảo: I thought he’d scold us, but Mr. Khải laughed and told us to leave the stain, so we’d remember today whenever we see it. On this lane, even spilled paint becomes a keepsake.
Cháu ơi, tối qua cả hẻm ngồi uống trà tr: Last night the whole lane sat drinking tea in front of my house, dear. Everyone said the corner of the lane looks so bare, just a power pole and a tangle of wires.
Bà mới nảy ra ý: mình trồng một giàn hoa: So I had an idea: let’s plant a bougainvillea arch there, so whoever comes home from work feels the lane welcoming them. The clockmaker will build the trellis, Thảo will choose the plants, and the painter will paint a name board.
Cả hẻm ai cũng góp một tay. Còn cháu, ch: Everyone is lending a hand. And you, dear, what would you like to bring?
Ngày Cả Hẻm Trồng Hoa: The Day the Lane Planted Flowers
Hôm nay cả hẻm trồng hoa giấy đó! Bác đồ: Today the whole lane planted bougainvillea! The clockmaker built the wooden arch, the painter hung up a “Bougainvillea Lane” sign, Minh and Mr. Khải dug the soil, and Ms. Hạnh taught us kids a song.
Còn Bánh Quy thì nằm lăn trên đống đất m: And Biscuit rolled around in the fresh soil and wouldn’t budge. Mum had to give him two baths!
Mấy tuần rồi, giàn hoa giấy đầu ngõ đã t: It’s been a few weeks, and the bougainvillea arch at the corner has its first pink clusters. Every afternoon I take a chair out there and watch everyone in the lane come home.
Hồi cháu mới dọn tới, căn gác chỉ có một: When you first moved in, the attic had one dusty window and every door on the lane was shut. Now the whole lane feels like a window thrown open.
Bà già rồi, chẳng biết nói gì hay. Chỉ m: I’m old and not good with words. I only want to thank you, dear, for opening that window first.
